source_text: Τὸ γὰρ ἀβούλητον ἢ ὡς ἄδικον αὐτῷ ἐστιν ἀβούλητον ἢ ὡς ἀνάξιον. Καὶ πάλιν τὸ ἄδικον ἢ περὶ αὐτὸν θεωρεῖται τὸν ἀναστησόμενον ἢ περὶ ἄλλον τινὰ παρ᾿ αὐτόν. Ἀλλ᾿ ὅτι μὲν οὐδεὶς ἀδικεῖται τῶν ἔξωθεν καὶ τῶν ἐν τοῖς οὖσιν ἀριθμουμένων, πρόδηλον. Οὔτε γὰρ αἱ νοηταὶ φύσεις ἐκ τῆς τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀναστάσεως ἀδικηθεῖεν ἄν· οὐδὲ γὰρ ἐμπόδιόν τι ταύταις πρὸς τὸ εἶναι, οὐ βλάβος οὐχ ὕβρις ἡ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀνάστασις· οὐ μὴν οὐδὲ τῶν ἀλόγων ἡ φύσις οὐδὲ τῶν ἀψύχων· οὐδὲ γὰρ ἔσται μετὰ τὴν ἀνάστασιν· περὶ δὲ τὸ μὴ ὄν οὐδὲν ἄδικον. Εἰ δὲ καὶ εἶναί τις ὑποθοῖτο διὰ παντός, οὐκ ἂν ἀδικηθείη ταῦτα, τῶν ἀνθρωπίνων σωμάτων ἀνανεωθέντων· εἰ γὰρ ὑπείκοντα νῦν τῇ φύσει τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ ταῖς τούτων χρείαις ὄντων ἐνδεῶν, ὑπό τε ζυγὸν ἠγμένα καὶ δουλείαν παντοίαν, οὐδὲν ἀδικεῖται, πολὺ μᾶλλον, ἀφθάρτων καὶ ἀνενδεῶν γενομένων καὶ μηκέτι δεομένων τῆς τούτων χρείας, ἐλευθερωθέντα δὲ πάσης δουλείας οὐκ ἀδικηθήσεται. Οὐδὲ γάρ, εἰ φωνῆς μετεῖχεν, ᾐτιάσατο ἂν τὸν δημιουργὸν ὡς παρὰ τὸ δίκαιον ἐλαττούμενα τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὅτι μὴ τῆς αὐτῆς τούτοις τετύχηκεν ἀναστάσεως. Ὧν γὰρ ἡ φύσις οὐκ ἴση, τούτοις οὐδὲ τὸ τέλος ἴσον ὁ δίκαιος ἐπιμετρεῖ. Χωρὶς δὲ τούτων, παρ᾿ οἷς οὐδεμία τοῦ δικαίου κρίσις οὐδὲ μέμψις ἀδικίας.Οὐ μὴν οὐδ᾿ ἐκεῖνο φῆσαι δυνατὸν ὡς περὶ αὐτὸν θεωρεῖταί τις ἀδικία τὸν ἀνιστάμενον ἄνθρωπον. Ἔστι μὲν γὰρ οὗτος ἐκ ψυχῆς καὶ σώματος, οὔτε δὲ εἰς ψυχὴν οὔτε εἰς σῶμα δέχεται τὴν ἀδικίαν. Οὔτε γὰρ τὴν ψυχὴν ἀδικεῖσθαι φήσει τις σωφρονῶν, ὅτι λήσεταί γε ταύτῃ συνεκβάλλων καὶ τὴν παροῦσαν ζωήν· εἰ γὰρ νῦν ἐν φθαρτῷ καὶ παθητῷ κατοικοῦσα σώματι μηδὲν ἠδίκηται, πολὺ μᾶλλον ἀφθάρτῳ καὶ ἀπαθεῖ συζῶσα οὐκ ἀδικηθήσεται. Ἀλλ᾿ οὐδὲ τὸ σῶμα ἀδικεῖταί τι· εἰ γὰρ νῦν φθαρτὸν ἀφθάρτῳ συνὸν οὐκ ἀδικεῖται, δῆλον ὅτι οὐδ᾿ ἄφθαρτον ἀφθάρτῳ συνὸν ἀδικηθήσεται. Οὐ μὴν οὐδ᾿ ἐκεῖνο φαίη τις ἂν ὡς ἀνάξιον ἔργον τοῦ θεοῦ τὸ διαλυθὲν ἀναστῆσαι σῶμα καὶ συναγαγεῖν· εἰ γὰρ τὸ χεῖρον οὐκ ἀνάξιον, τοῦτ᾿ ἔστι τὸ φθαρτὸν ποιῆσαι σῶμα καὶ παθητόν, πολὺ μᾶλλον τὸ κρεῖττον οὐκ ἀνάξιον, ὅπερ ἐστὶν ἄφθαρτον καὶ ἀπαθές.
thought_title: No injustice or unworthiness in resurrection
orientation: Athenagoras is arguing that resurrection is not unwilled by God, and now shows that it is neither unjust nor unworthy of God, first with respect to other beings and then with respect to the human being raised.
pass_a_gloss: For the unwilled is unwilled for him either as unjust or as unworthy. And again the unjust is considered either with respect to the one who will be raised himself or with respect to some other besides him. But that no one of those outside and of those numbered among the things that exist is wronged, is clear. For neither would the intelligible natures be wronged by the resurrection of humans; for the resurrection of humans is not any hindrance to them for being, not harm, not outrage; nor indeed the nature of the irrational creatures nor of the lifeless things; for they will not be after the resurrection; and concerning what is not, nothing is unjust. But if someone should suppose that they exist forever, these things would not be wronged, when the human bodies have been renewed; for if now yielding to the nature of humans and to the needs of these, being in need, and having been brought under yoke and slavery of every kind, they are not wronged at all, much more, when humans have become incorruptible and without need and no longer need the use of these things, and these things have been freed from all slavery, they will not be wronged. For not even, if they had a share of voice, would they have accused the creator as being diminished beyond what is just in comparison with humans, because they have not obtained the same resurrection as these. For to those whose nature is not equal, to these the just one does not measure out an equal end either. And apart from these things, among whom there is no judgment of what is just nor any blame of injustice. Nor indeed is it possible to say that some injustice is considered with respect to the one who is raised, the human being himself. For this one is from soul and body, and he receives the injustice neither into soul nor into body. For no one being of sound mind will say that the soul is wronged, because he will forget at least, casting out together with it also the present life; for if now dwelling in a corruptible and passible body it has been wronged in nothing, much more living together with an incorruptible and impassible body it will not be wronged. But neither is the body wronged in anything; for if now being corruptible and being together with an incorruptible thing it is not wronged, it is clear that neither will it be wronged being incorruptible and being together with an incorruptible thing. Nor indeed would anyone say that to raise the dissolved body and to gather it together is an unworthy work of God; for if the worse is not unworthy, that is, to make a corruptible and passible body, much more the better is not unworthy, which is incorruptible and impassible.

choices.why: The brief's argument uses 'unwilled' as the opposite of God's will; keeping the privative adjective preserves the technical force of the argument.
The potential optative with ἄν expresses a hypothetical possibility; 'would be wronged' keeps the conditional force.
The aorist passive participle in the genitive absolute construction is rendered as a finite clause in English to preserve the temporal/causal sense.
The brief's glossary fixes 'incorruptibility' for ἀφθαρσία; 'impassible' is the standard philosophical term for ἀπαθής, not subject to suffering.
The compound verb means casting out along with; the gloss keeps the 'together' force of συν-.
The verb means to measure out or apportion; 'measures out' preserves the distributive sense of the just one assigning ends.

pass_b_english: For what is unwilled is unwilled either because it is unjust to him or because it is unworthy of him. And again, what is unjust is considered either with respect to the one who will be raised himself or with respect to someone else besides him. Now it is clear that none of those outside and numbered among existing things is wronged. For neither would the intelligible natures be wronged by the resurrection of human beings—the resurrection of human beings is no hindrance to their existence, no harm, no outrage—nor indeed would the nature of irrational creatures or of lifeless things be wronged, for they will not exist after the resurrection, and nothing unjust can be done to what does not exist. But even if someone should suppose that they exist forever, they would not be wronged when human bodies have been renewed. For if now, yielding to the nature of human beings and to their needs when they are in want, they are brought under the yoke and into every kind of slavery and are not wronged, much more, when human beings have become incorruptible and free from need and no longer require their service, and they themselves have been released from all slavery, they will not be wronged. For if they had a voice, they would not accuse the Creator of being unjustly diminished in comparison with human beings because they did not obtain the same resurrection as these. For where the nature is not equal, the Just One does not measure out an equal end. And apart from these things, among beings that have no judgment of what is just and no accusation of injustice, there is no wrong.

Nor indeed is it possible to say that some injustice is considered with respect to the human being who is raised himself. For this being is composed of soul and body, and the injustice attaches neither to the soul nor to the body. No one in his right mind will say that the soul is wronged, for in doing so he will inadvertently cast out the present life as well. For if the soul now dwelling in a corruptible and passible body is not wronged, much more will it not be wronged when she lives together with an incorruptible and impassible body. But neither is the body wronged at all. For if now, being corruptible, it is joined to the incorruptible and is not wronged, it is clear that when it is incorruptible and joined to the incorruptible, it will not be wronged. Nor indeed would anyone say that it is an unworthy work of God to raise up and gather together the body that has been dissolved. For if the worse thing is not unworthy—that is, making a corruptible and passible body—much more is the better thing not unworthy, which is incorruptibility and impassibility.

problems.quote: being corruptible and joined to what is incorruptible
problems.why: The Greek says 'being corruptible, joined to the incorruptible' (i.e., soul); English reverses: body is corruptible joined to incorruptible soul. But 'what is incorruptible' obscures that it's the soul.
problems.fix: the body, being corruptible, joined to the incorruptible

edits.old: For if now, being corruptible and joined to what is incorruptible, it is not wronged, it is clear that when it is incorruptible and joined to what is incorruptible, it will not be wronged.
edits.new: For if now, being corruptible and joined to the incorruptible, it is not wronged, it is clear that when it is incorruptible and joined to the incorruptible, it will not be wronged.

problems.quote: For if they had a voice, they would not accuse the Creator of being diminished unjustly in comparison with human beings
problems.source_quote: Οὐδὲ γάρ, εἰ φωνῆς μετεῖχεν, ᾐτιάσατο ἂν τὸν δημιουργὸν ὡς παρὰ τὸ δίκαιον ἐλαττούμενα τῶν ἀνθρώπων
problems.why: ἐλαττούμενα modifies the animals (neuter plural), not the Creator; they are diminished relative to humans, not accusing the Creator of being diminished.
problems.fix: For if they had a voice, they would not accuse the Creator of being unjustly diminished in comparison with human beings

problems.quote: No one in his right mind will say that the soul is wronged, because he would be casting out along with it the present life as well
problems.source_quote: ὅτι λήσεταί γε ταύτῃ συνεκβάλλων καὶ τὴν παροῦσαν ζωήν
problems.why: λήσεταί γε ταύτῃ συνεκβάλλων means 'he will inadvertently cast out along with it,' not 'he would be casting out'; the Greek warns of an unintended consequence, not a deliberate act.
problems.fix: No one in his right mind will say that the soul is wronged, for in doing so he will inadvertently cast out the present life as well

problems.quote: the just one does not measure out an equal end
problems.why: ὁ δίκαιος refers to God as 'the Just One,' a title; 'the just one' as generic is weak and misses the theological point.
problems.fix: the Just One does not measure out an equal end

problems.quote: when it lives together with an incorruptible and impassible body
problems.why: συζῶσα is feminine singular, referring to the soul living with the body; 'it' is ambiguous and could refer to the body. The soul is the subject.
problems.fix: when she lives together with an incorruptible and impassible body

problems.quote: if now, being corruptible and joined to the incorruptible, it is not wronged
problems.source_quote: εἰ γὰρ νῦν φθαρτὸν ἀφθάρτῳ συνὸν οὐκ ἀδικεῖται
problems.why: The body is corruptible joined to the incorruptible soul now; 'being corruptible and joined to the incorruptible' misorders: it is the corruptible (body) joined to the incorruptible (soul), not both adjectives describing one thing.
problems.fix: if now, being corruptible, it is joined to the incorruptible and is not wronged

problems.quote: which is an incorruptible and impassible body
problems.why: ὅπερ ἐστὶν ἄφθαρτον καὶ ἀπαθές refers back to τὸ κρεῖττον ('the better thing'), not a body; it is the state of incorruptibility and impassibility, not 'an incorruptible and impassible body.'

edits.new: For if they had a voice, they would not accuse the Creator of being unjustly diminished in comparison with human beings

problems.quote: much more, when human beings have become incorruptible and free from need and no longer require their service, and they themselves have been released from all slavery, will they not be wronged.
problems.source_quote: πολὺ μᾶλλον, ἀφθάρτων καὶ ἀνενδεῶν γενομένων καὶ μηκέτι δεομένων τῆς τούτων χρείας, ἐλευθερωθέντα δὲ πάσης δουλείας οὐκ ἀδικηθήσεται.
problems.why: Source says 'will not be wronged' (οὐκ ἀδικηθήσεται), a statement. English renders it as a question 'will they not be wronged?', flipping the sense.
problems.fix: much more, when human beings have become incorruptible and free from need and no longer require their service, and they themselves have been released from all slavery, they will not be wronged.
problems.ruling: οὐκ ἀδικηθήσεται is declarative 'will not be wronged'; English question 'will they not be wronged?' inverts to rhetorical question expecting 'yes they will', reversing meaning.

edits.old: much more, when human beings have become incorruptible and free from need and no longer require their service, and they themselves have been released from all slavery, will they not be wronged.
edits.new: much more, when human beings have become incorruptible and free from need and no longer require their service, and they themselves have been released from all slavery, they will not be wronged.

fixed: The question mark issue was real; changed 'will they not be wronged?' to a statement 'they will not be wronged' to match the source.

dismissed.why: συνεκβάλλων means 'cast out together with it', not 'inadvertently'
dismissed.note: λήσεται + participle = 'will unawares cast out', so 'inadvertently' is exactly right and 'as well' renders συν-.

dismissed.why: Greek has neuter adjectives 'incorruptible and impassible', not abstract nouns
dismissed.note: Abstract nouns vs neuter adjectives is style; sense (the better thing is an incorruptible, impassible body) survives.
